data.headline: Thirty-year Treasury yield edges down to 5.40%
data.summary: The 30-year Treasury yield fell one basis point on Thursday, from 5.41% to 5.40%. The ten-year yield dropped three basis points to 5.04%, leaving the long end 36 basis points above the ten-year benchmark.

bull.text: The decline in the 30-year benchmark supported long-duration bond prices, all else equal.

bear.text: Leveraged funds held a net short position of 149,858 Treasury bond futures contracts on November 10. They had been net short 166,257 a week earlier.

watch.text: The gap between the 30-year and ten-year yields widened from 34 basis points on Wednesday to 36 on Thursday. Further changes matter to a fund concentrated in longer maturities.

limitations: Treasury par yields describe constant maturities. TLT holds a portfolio of bonds, and its realized session return also depends on its market prices and any distributions. The futures positions predate Thursday’s yield observations.
